courses.title: Accounting for Agribusiness I
courses.description: Presentation of the underlying framework and concepts of financial accounting used by businesses and organizations in the food and agribusiness industries. Students learn how accounting information is collected and organized to evaluate the performance and financial status of organizations. Topics include the basics of recording transactions as well as accounting for assets, liabilities, owner’s equity, cash flows, revenue and net income. Additionally, students will learn the preparation of financial statements using generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP).

courses.title: Agricultural Water Resource Management
courses.description: Water resource management applied to current issues. Water delivery systems in the United States and California, survey of water rights, water pollution, water conservation, food and agricultural system water use, and efficient water management. Includes water problems in developing nations.

courses.title: Agriculture: The Foundation of Civilizations
courses.description: [GE 3B] Introduction to the genesis and evolution of agriculture as the foundation of civilizations throughout history. Analyzing agriculture within the context of the development and evolution of various civilizations over time. Emphasis on critical analysis of the historical development of agriculture in various parts of the world including the United States using documentary and literature collections. Open to all majors. Required of all College of Agriculture majors.

courses.title: Global Resources for Food
courses.description: [GE 4A] Examine the resource base for agricultural production on various continents, and whether there is potential for increasing food supplies. The role of agriculture in economic development will be addressed.

courses.title: Ethical Issues in Food, Agricultural and Apparel Industries
courses.description: [GE 3C or 4C] Socioeconomic and scientific issues in the Food, Agricultural, and Apparel Systems within a framework of moral philosophy and ethical reasoning. Analysis of topics in biotechnology in agricultural and apparel production, food processing, intellectual property rights, food safety, nutrition, the treatment of animals, the environment, labor rights in a global marketplace, and reducing world hunger and malnutrition.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Development of Leadership Skills In Agriculture
courses.description: The exploration of professional growth and leadership development in the context of food and agriculture careers. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Orientation to Agricultural Science
courses.description: Outline the academic path that students will follow to be successful in this major. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. Cover campus life, university rules, policies and regulations. Mandatory fall quarter course for entering freshmen. Strategies to assist students with the transition from school to university and the successful completion of their college career in the Agricultural Science department. Topics covered include: campus student support services, career planning, time management, academic planning, study/note/test skills, learning styles, navigating the college and university, professional development, extracurricular activities, and others.

courses.title: Advocacy in Agricultural Science
courses.description: Overview of agriculture programs including goals and purposes of all educational levels of education in agriculture. Course focuses on developing students’ abilities in presenting personal and researched views of the agricultural industry and developing students ability to advocate for the industry as a whole.

courses.title: Senior Project
courses.description: Selection and completion of a project under faculty supervision. Projects typical of problems which graduates must solve in their fields of employment. Project results are presented in a formal report.

courses.title: Culture, People, and Dress
courses.description: [GE 4A] Study of the interrelatedness of socio-psychological, economic and political/religious influences on dress in a historical perspective. Cross-cultural analysis and interpretation of Western and non-Western clothing behavior through written analysis papers.

courses.title: Food Animal Production
courses.description: A study of the domestic livestock industry and animal management techniques emphasizing the importance of management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, selection, breeding principles and disease control to ensure scientifically based management decisions.

courses.title: Companion, Laboratory and Exotic Animal Care
courses.description: General concepts of handling and restraining domestic and exotic animals. Emphasis will be placed on behavior, management, nutrition, disease prevention, and breed identification. The care and use of laboratory animals will be covered in depth.

courses.title: Food Animal Production Laboratory
courses.description: A study of the commonly applied animal techniques and practices used to scientifically manage livestock in the commercial food animal industry. The laboratory will emphasize the importance of evaluating business management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, genetics and selection, breeding principles and herd health plans in order of evaluate scientifically based domestic animal livestock management methodologies. Product fee required.

courses.title: Drugs and Society
courses.description: Identification and explanation of the action of different drugs. The compounds discussed include over-the-counter drugs, prescription drugs, social drugs, and drugs of abuse. How addictions develop, why they are harmful, and how to stop them. Emphasizes human pharmacology although the principles are the same for animals.

courses.title: Animal Industry and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of the application of science in the food animal industry and animal production systems, the role and use of food animals and animal products in resolving problems associated with humanity, and the influence of animal agriculture on history, civilization and human values.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Meat Science
courses.description: Introduction to processing and utilization of fresh and value-added red meat products. Discussions on identity standards, factors affecting sensory, nutritional and shelf-life quality attributes, food safety (microbiological, chemical and physical hazards), including inspection and grading of red meats.

courses.title: Biology and Society
courses.description: [GE 5B] Fundamental concepts in biology are taught using socially relevant themes. Biological concepts are related to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow, exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigations, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society.

courses.title: Biology and Society Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] A laboratory support course applying lecture concepts through hands-on, inquiry-based, learn-by-doing approaches. Supports students in majors that require fundamental concepts of biology as they relate to the major themes of evolution; structure and function; information flow exchange and storage; transformations of energy and matter; and systems. Uses the study of biology to illustrate science as a way of knowing, the methods and practices of science, limits of scientific endeavors, ethics associated with biological investigation, and how biology can help inform decisions we make as individuals and as a society. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1110 or BIO 1150 ; BIO 1150 can be concurrent. Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: [GE 5C] Laboratory experiments to illustrate and enhance lecture topics in CHM 1210 . Basic laboratory techniques and practices. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210 .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Introduction to Food Science and Technology
courses.description: An introduction to the scope, principles and practices of food science and technology. Basic aspects of chemistry, microbiology and sensory analysis of food products. Introduction to food packaging, safety and sanitation and basics of food laws and regulations. Principles of food engineering and the most common methods of food preservation. Overview on sustainability and the commercial processing of specific food commodities.

courses.title: Food Safety and Current Issues
courses.description: [GE 5D] Overview of physical, chemical and microbiological hazards and their role in foodborne illness and the safety of the food supply. Introduction to the Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point System. The role of government and basic aspects of food safety laws and regulations. Review of current issues in food safety, food protection, food production, and food processing as they relate to public health.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Ethnic Studies of Food, Nutrition, and Health Disparities
courses.description: [GE 6] Cross Listed as: EWS 2180 Interdisciplinary study of Native American, African American, Asian American, and/or Latina and Latino American communities and food, nutrition, and health inequities in the United States. Foundational theoretical concepts of ethnic studies and nutrition such as racism, colonialism, immigration, eurocentrism, social determinants of health, food and health disparities, acculturation, and health equity are examined.

courses.title: Food and Culture
courses.description: [GE 4C] Interrelationship of food availability, historical developments, socio-economic institutions, political, religious, and other influences on food patterns. In-depth study of a selected culture.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Horticulture and Greenhouse Management
courses.description: Explore the fascinating world of plants and the intricate processes governing their growth, development, and interactions with the environment. An introduction to Plant Science that provides a comprehensive understanding of the biological, chemical, and physical principles that support plant life and cultivation. Emphasis is placed on plant anatomy, physiology, reproduction, taxonomy, soil science, and sustainable production practices. Gain a foundation for advanced studies in plant science, horticulture, and sustainable agriculture. Corequisite(s): PLT 1120L .

courses.title: Horticulture and Greenhouse Management
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental principles and practices of horticulture in landscape, greenhouse, and controlled environment systems. Emphasis on plant identification, anatomy, and physiology, along with applied skills in propagation, pruning, soils, irrigation, hydroponics, pest management, turfgrass, and nursery/greenhouse operations. Gain hands-on experience through laboratory and field activities designed to prepare for careers in horticulture and plant science. Corequisite(s): PLT 1120 .

courses.title: Agronomy and Farm Management
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of crop production and management, exploring environmental and economic factors that shape agriculture. Delve into crop biology, soil health, and pest management, with a strong focus on sustainable practices and innovations. Highlighting modern techniques like precision agriculture and biotechnology to address critical challenges such as climate change and global food security. Corequisite(s): PLT 1130L .

courses.title: Agronomy and Farm Management Laboratory
courses.description: Hands-on experiences that complement the lecture component. Engage in practical activities related to crop production, soil health, and pest management. Through experiments and fieldwork, develop essential skills in crop assessment and sustainable practices, applying scientific principles to real-world agricultural challenges. Corequisite(s): PLT 1130 .

courses.title: History of Garden Art
courses.description: [GE 3A] The relationship of ornamental flora to the human living experience to show the continuity with contemporary gardens, homes, parks and other art. An introduction to the various styles in landscape art as they developed in different cultures and in preceding ages.

courses.title: Insects and Civilization
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of insects and related arthropods and their influence on life, ranging from everyday events to how they have changed the history of the world. Selected topics on the importance of arthropods in modern and ancient cultures. Course synthesizes biological and historical topics related to arthropods in context of major world events and cultures both past and present, fields of study including science and technology, medicine, world hunger relief, and others. Open to all majors. Open to all majors.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650L .

courses.title: Sustainable Agriculture Laboratory
courses.description: Current advances, issues and future directions in agriculture to ensure the long-term economic prosperity, environmental preservation, and social equity of food, fuel and fiber production. Corequisite(s): PLT 3650 .

courses.title: Introduction to Regenerative Studies
courses.description: A survey of interactions between physical, biological and social systems essential for human life, including food, water, energy, shelter and waste management. Development of conscious understanding of the relationship between people and their social and physical environments, through examination of systems that sustain future generations through the regeneration of critical resources and ecosystem processes.

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Undergraduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
